requirement:
The returned `OutlineContent` and its clones remain usable after the cache
has been dropped. They share the snapshot described in
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`.
rationale:
structural: The structural obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.outline_file.lifetime` is that the returned `OutlineContent` and its clones are usable after the cache is dropped, and that they share the snapshot. An alternative that borrows from the cache, or deep-copies per clone, would break that. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#struct[OutlineContent]` satisfies this. It is `#[derive(Clone)]` and holds an owned `snapshot: Arc<Snapshot>` with no borrow of the cache, so clones share one snapshot. `Snapshot` owns its source (`Arc<str>`), outline, children, language and scheme, and `impl[OutlineContent]/fn[prepare]` builds it with `Arc::new`. The root carries the `{impl}` marker, and the code behind it backs the marker. The retained-parts content of `requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot` is only cited, so it needs no coverage here.

behavioral: The requirement has one behavioral obligation. A returned `OutlineContent` and its clones must stay usable after the cache is dropped, and they share the snapshot described in `requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`. The snapshot requirement is cited, not subject to reassessment here.

The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[domain_clones_share_the_first_successful_outline_for_each_path]` covers it:
- It moves the cache into `domain`, clones that into `peer`, and drops both with `drop(domain)` and `drop(peer)`. `fresh` came from a temporary `Application::default()` cache that is also gone.
- It then deletes the source file from disk. A value that re-read the file or depended on the cache would fail from this point.
- It takes `retained = cached.clone()`, drops `cached` and `snapshot`, and asserts `retained.select("fn[first]").unwrap().text() == "fn first() {}"`. That is the original snapshot text, not the later `fn second() {}` content. So the clone stays usable after the cache is dropped and after the file is gone.
- Sharing is supported by `ptr::eq(snapshot.outline(), cached.outline())`, plus equal text, fingerprint and structural hash between values returned for the same path.

The test never uses the original returned value after the cache is dropped. It uses a clone instead. It also never asserts pointer identity between a clone and its source. I don't count either as a gap. If `OutlineContent` borrowed from the cache, dropping the cache while `cached` and `snapshot` were still alive would not compile. The clone's post-drop content matches the snapshot, and the file deletion rules out re-reading. Detailed snapshot properties belong to `requirements.sdk.outlines.snapshot`.

An `OutlineContent` retains the source text, outline, and selected language's
fingerprinting scheme describing that same snapshot. Its item spans, selected
text, and structural hashes are derived from those bytes. A cached value keeps
these parts together; later file edits do not change the loaded value.
